title: Six Friends, Three Bowls, One Very Long Climb: The History of the Buckaroo Football League
dek: From a founding season without a single trade to the Habibsters dynasty and the most unlikely worst-to-first run the league has ever seen, this is how the Buckaroo Football League became what it is.
body: The Buckaroo Football League kicked off on ESPN in 2023 with six teams and six managers who all grew up in Chicago. That meant Bears misery and Packers trash talk came built in. What did not come built in was any willingness to deal: the league went the entire inaugural season without a single trade. Everybody drafted, everybody clutched their rosters, and everybody found out together.

Kaushal's Habibsters set the tone at 10-4, taking the top seed with 1,528.8 points. Alan's Team Pillbert went 9-5 for the second seed, powered in part by the best single week of the year, a 156.18 in week 3 against Sonny. The most telling number of the season belonged to Mekhi, though. Dawgs scored a league-high 1,542.8 points and still finished 6-8, the first chapter in what would become a long book of Kai getting nothing for his trouble.

The playoffs were two-week totals, and Habib handled both rounds. Habibsters beat Dawgs 237.54 to 196.12 in the semifinal while Philly got past Randy's The fumblers 234.86 to 216.44. Then came Buckaroo Bowl I, and it was not close: Habibsters 251.36, Team Pillbert 192.08. The league had its first champion and, as it turned out, the start of a habit.

At the other end, Ramon's Araleasers posted the worst record at 4-10 and the season's lowest week, a 65.9 in week 9. But last place is decided by a consolation ladder, and that ladder dropped Sonny's Ben Dover, a 6-8 team, into sixth place. The man who built the league finished at the bottom of it.

If 2023 was a statement, 2024 was a coronation. Habibsters went 11-3 and grabbed the top seed again, and Kaushal worked the waiver wire like it owed him money, making 32 pickups. The league, meanwhile, made zero trades for the second straight year. Two full seasons, not one deal. Historians will study this.

The season opened with a bang from an unlikely source. Ramon's Araleasers dropped 166.58 points in week 1 against Sonny, the highest week of the year, and rode that energy to a 7-7 record and the third seed while making exactly one pickup all season. Randy's The fumblers, meanwhile, led the league with 1,595.1 points and went 8-6 for the second seed. Randy's 162.5 in week 3 came against Brucie, too, which made what happened next sting even more.

In the semifinals, Araleasers knocked off The fumblers 202.44 to 176.14, sending the league's highest-scoring team out early. Habibsters handled Team Pillbert 296.96 to 245.08 on the other side. In Buckaroo Bowl II, Habib's crew crushed Araleasers 261.44 to 145.28. Back-to-back titles, a 4-0 playoff run across two years, and a growing sense around the league that the trophy simply lived at Kaushal's place.

Sonny, for his part, had a season to forget. Ben Dover went 5-9 with a league-low 1,304.3 points, bottoming out with a 44.1 in week 12 against Mekhi, the lowest single week of the year. He made one pickup all season. Second straight last-place finish. Nobody at the time could have guessed what came next.

The 2025 season expanded to a longer schedule, and Sonny treated it like a new game entirely. After making one pickup the year before, he made 22, and he also made his first trade. Ben Dover went 13-3, scored 1,850.8 points, and took the top seed, with a season-best 153.4 in week 10 against Randy along the way. Two years of last place, then the best record the league had ever seen.

Randy finally got his deep playoff run. The fumblers went 9-7 for the second seed and then demolished Habibsters 137.1 to 79.96 in the semifinal, the first time anyone had beaten Kaushal in the postseason. Habib's team had led the entire league with 1,973.6 points but finished just 8-8, a reminder that points and wins do not always talk to each other.

Buckaroo Bowl III was a one-week affair, and Ben Dover won it 105.1 to 86.48 over The fumblers. Worst to first, completed. Sonny went from back-to-back last-place finishes to champion in a single season, and his playoff record now sits at a perfect 1-0. For Randy, it was a third straight playoff appearance and a third straight year without the trophy.

The strangest storyline of 2025 had nothing to do with the standings at the top. Ramon ran Araleasers through week 8, then was kicked from the league for inactivity. The team was renamed Ramon's Remains and played on without him, and in its very first game without Brucie in charge it beat Alan 94.76 to 92.02 in week 9. Those games still count on Ramon's record, asterisk and all, and the league has never let him forget that his abandoned roster kept winning.

Araleasers and Ramon's Remains also somehow became the trade hub of the league. There were four trades in 2025, and Ramon's team was part of every single one of them. After two seasons in which nobody traded at all, the busiest dealer in the league turned out to be a team that spent half the year without a manager.

Then there was Mekhi. Kai drafted from basic training, still put up 1,858.2 points, second only to Habib, and posted the season's best week with a 153.62 in week 9 against Randy. Dawgs finished 8-8 as the fourth seed. And then the consolation ladder did its thing, and Dawgs finished sixth of six. Few managers in this league know more football, and few have less to show for it on paper.

Three seasons of matchups have carved out some real grudges. The loudest one belongs to Kaushal and Alan: Habib is 7-1 against Philly all time, including the Buckaroo Bowl I rout and the 2024 semifinal. Kaushal is also 8-2 against Mekhi and 8-3 against Ramon. Only one manager owns a winning record against Habib, and it is Randy, at 6-4, which may be the only thing standing between Kaushal and total dominance of the ledger.

Randy has his own victims. He is 7-3 against Ramon, though Brucie got the one that mattered most in the 2024 semifinal. Alan, meanwhile, holds a 7-5 edge on Randy, and Sonny is 7-4 against Ramon. Some matchups are dead even: Sonny and Alan are 5-5, and so are Alan and Ramon. Those are the games where nobody gets bragging rights for long.

The postseason tells its own story. Kaushal is 4-1 in the playoffs with two titles. Randy has made the playoffs every year but is 1-3 once he gets there. Alan is 1-2, Ramon is 1-1, Mekhi is 0-1, and Sonny is 1-0 with a ring. One dynasty, one redemption, and a lot of people still waiting.

In 2026 the league grew from six teams to eight, adding Jordan and Zoe. JMoney runs Counting or not Counting GV, and Zoe, in her first season of fantasy football and the lone non-Chicagoan in the group, runs Ghostu-Spider SZN. For the first time, someone in this league can defend the Packers without being outnumbered five to one. Well, seven to one now.

The familiar faces are back under new banners and old ones. Sonny defends his title with The Horse is Hea, Ramon returns with No Banner only HULK, and Habibsters, Team Pillbert, The fumblers and Dawgs are all chasing the same trophy. Kai, true to form, drafted from overseas this time.

That season is still being played. Habib wants his third, Sonny wants to prove 2025 was no fluke, Randy and Philly want their first, and two rookies want to crash the whole thing. The road to Buckaroo Bowl IV is open.
